explanations: luna: The verse says that those who follow God's guidance need not fear; it specifically joins following (اتبَعَ) with guidance, the section's image of staying behind a guide on the road. | terra: After the descent, whoever follows God's guidance need not fear or grieve. It adds the ongoing act of following to the section's request to be led.

luna: As the prompt's example indicates, ضل سواء السبيل directly makes straying a loss of the road's middle; the context warns against exchanging faith for disbelief. | terra: It says the person who exchanges faith for disbelief has gone astray from sawāʾ al-sabīl. The exact middle-of-the-road expression reverses Moses' request in 28:22.

luna: In the dispute over the direction of prayer, the verse says God guides whom He wills to a straight path; a changed direction makes the route's divine guidance concrete. | terra: God guides whom He wills to a straight path; its exact path-and-guidance formulation carries the Fatiha petition into the change of qibla.
luna: The source section's dictionary sense of مَلِك الطريق is the road's middle; this verse calls the Muslim community أمة وسطا, a centered community, though it is not literally describing a road.

terra: When told to follow what God sent down, they insist on following what they found their fathers upon, even if those fathers lacked guidance. It tests inherited custom against a genuinely guided track.

luna: During the Hajj route from Arafat to the sacred landmark, people are told to remember how God guided them, though before that they were among the lost; this ties finding one's way to a named destination.

luna: After people differ, God guides believers to the truth by His permission and guides whom He wills to a straight path; it links the path with resolving division. | terra: After human beings become divided, God guides believers to the truth they dispute by His permission, to a straight path. It places a single guided route after communal division.

luna: After distinguishing right guidance from error, the verse describes holding to the firm handhold that does not break; this gives a specific image of remaining attached to guidance, though it is not itself a road.

luna: The verse describes God bringing believers from darkness into light while unbelievers' patrons bring them from light into darkness; this is a specific reversal of the section's request for a guide toward the right way.
luna: The prayer asks God not to let hearts deviate after guidance; it parallels the section's request to stay straight on a path already shown.

luna: The section notes that worship and the walked road remain distinct senses in one word family; this verse explicitly places worship of God beside “this is a straight path.” | terra: Jesus joins worship of the one Lord to the declaration that this is a straight path, making na'budu's worship the way itself.

luna: The verse joins holding fast to God with being guided إلى صراط مستقيم, linking continued adherence to arrival on the straight path. | terra: Holding fast to God is followed by being guided to a straight path, joining a sustaining grip to the continued route requested in the section.

luna: The community is commanded to hold together by God's rope and not disperse; this makes the section's contrast between a common road and people scattering in every direction concrete. | terra: The community is told to hold God's rope all together and not become divided. Its shared holding gives a communal counterpoint to the section's people scattering in every direction.
terra: God promises to make clear and guide believers in the sunan of those before them. These prior courses specify the idea of a route already trodden by earlier people.
luna: The verse says some recipients of scripture choose error and want others to stray from the way; it stages people trying to divert travelers from their route.

luna: Obedience to God and the Messenger is followed by guidance to a straight path; it depicts how one comes to walk the road. | terra: Obedience to God and the Messenger would bring the promise of guidance to a straight path; the verse makes following the leader a route to that path.

luna: The source section's صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم (“the path of those You favored”) is named again here: those favored are prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous, and they are good companions on the way. | terra: It identifies the obedient as being with those upon whom God bestowed favor, including prophets and the righteous. It concretely identifies the favored company in Fatiha 1:7, after 4:68's path.

luna: The section pictures a path belonging to a favored community; this verse warns against opposing the Messenger and following a path other than that of the believers. | terra: One who follows a course other than the believers' way is turned toward what he chose. It gives a boundary for the section's shared community path.
terra: Those who hold fast to God receive mercy and are guided to Him on a straight path; the endpoint and route remain together.
luna: The covenant is followed by a warning that whoever disbelieves has strayed from سواء السبيل, the middle of the way named in the section's dictionary note.

luna: The section asks to be led on a straight path; here revelation guides followers of God's good pleasure through سبل السلام and then to a straight path. | terra: God guides those seeking His pleasure along paths of peace and out of darkness, then to a straight path; it makes guidance an actual passage with a destination.

luna: The verse names a law and a way (شرعة ومنهاجا) for each community, then calls them to race toward good; it makes a community's practiced course explicit, while recognizing distinct communities. | terra: God assigns each community a law and an open way, while saying He could have made them one community. The distinct communal routes sharpen the section's concern with a shared dīn and the danger of fragmentation.

luna: The verse warns against following desires of people who strayed and led many astray from سواء السبيل; it combines losing the center with bad leadership. | terra: Those who lead others astray are said to have strayed from sawāʾ al-sabīl. It is the same road-middle vocabulary as 28:22, now as a missed line.

terra: The reply that what the fathers practiced is enough is challenged by their lack of knowledge and guidance. It is a second explicit boundary between habitual inheritance and a route actually shown.

luna: People who reject the signs are described as deaf and dumb in darkness; God may leave one astray or place one on a straight path, a direct contrast of routes. | terra: God may leave someone in darkness or set that person on a straight path. The paired placement makes the path a condition one is put upon, not merely knows about.
luna: The signs are made clear so the way of criminals becomes distinct; the verse makes the wrong path recognizable by contrast.

luna: The section's lost traveler is staged directly: a man is حيران in the land while companions call him إلى الهدى; their call contrasts with the devils' diversion. | terra: It stages the bewildered person in the earth, with companions calling him back to guidance; this is the section's dalle fi al-ard scene and its communal answer.

luna: After listing prophets and their kin, the verse says God chose and guided them to a straight path; it links a community and its lineage to the traveled way. | terra: After naming a gathered line of prophets and their fathers and descendants, the verse says God chose and guided them to a straight path: a predecessor community already walking it.

luna: After naming earlier prophets, the verse says God guided them and commands the Prophet to follow their guidance; it concretely supplies predecessors whose path can be followed. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to follow the guidance of the preceding prophets. It is an explicit Quranic version of walking a route already made by those before.

luna: Stars are made as signs by which people find their way through land and sea darkness; this is the same navigation-by-signs relation developed from ع ل م in the section. | terra: The stars are made so people can be guided through the darknesses of land and sea, extending the section's landmark-and-navigation scene beyond 16:16.
luna: Following most people would lead the hearer away from God's way because they follow conjecture; it warns that the well-trodden route can be the wrong one.

luna: “This is your Lord's straight path” is followed by the claim that signs have been made clear; this ties the road to the signs by which it is recognized. | terra: God calls this the straight path of your Lord and says the signs have been detailed for a people who remember, linking a road with the signs that make it legible.

luna: The section's dictionary form صراط (ṣirāṭ) is the walked road; this verse calls God's way a straight path, commands following it, and contrasts it with plural ways that divide travelers from it. | terra: It names God's single straight path, commands following it, and makes the competing paths disperse walkers from it; this is the section's shared, trodden route versus people going apart.
luna: Those who split their religion and become factions are separated from the Prophet; this directly matches the section's dispersed groups as the opposite of a shared path.

luna: The Prophet is told to say his Lord guided him to a straight path, a sound religion; the verse brings guidance, the path, and dīn together as the section does. | terra: The Prophet says his Lord guided him to a straight path, an upright dīn; it joins hidaya, sirat, the section's dīn, and q-w-m straightness in one claim.

luna: Iblis says he will lie in wait on God's straight path; the verse makes the road itself the site of opposition to those who follow it. | terra: Iblis vows to sit upon God's straight path for people. The road is not empty: the lost-way danger takes the form of an ambush on the very route requested in Fatiha.

luna: The verse continues Iblis's ambush from front, back, right, and left; these approaches show opposition surrounding the straight route named in 7:16. | terra: It specifies the attack as from before, behind, right, and left. As the continuation of 7:16, its four directions surround the section's straight traveler without replacing the road itself.
luna: The people of the Garden say “He guided us to this”; their arrival at a destination through divine guidance makes the section's road-to-home gloss concrete.

luna: This verse places people on every road to threaten travelers, block God's way, and seek عوجا (crookedness); it reverses the section's open, straight communal road. | terra: The people are forbidden to sit on every road threatening travelers, blocking God's way, and seeking it crooked. It reverses the guide and landmark scene into obstruction and distortion.

luna: The verse contrasts taking سبيل الرشد with taking سبيل الغي; it makes the section's straight path and its opposite into two chosen routes. | terra: Those who reject God's signs do not take the way of right conduct when they see it, but take the way of error. The verse makes the divergent choice between visible routes explicit.
luna: The verse identifies the Messenger and says his followers follow the light sent with him; it stages the section's guide and the people walking after him.
terra: The universal Messenger is to be believed and followed so that people may be guided. It specifies the follower's response to the guide-speaker developed in the section.
terra: Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and judges with it. It supplies a qawm whose collective activity is guidance, rather than merely being guided.
terra: A community created by God guides by truth and acts justly with it. Its corporate guidance extends the section's association of a road with a people.
luna: The first emigrants and helpers are followed by those who follow them well; this gives a concrete succession of communities along the favored path.

luna: The section's dictionary definition of hidaya names both road and destination; God calls people to دار السلام and guides whom He wills to a straight path. | terra: God calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, making hidaya show both the route and the destination or home.

luna: The verse asks whether the one who guides to truth is more worthy to be followed; it directly joins the section's guide going ahead with the traveler's act of following. | terra: The question contrasts one who guides to truth with one unable to guide unless guided. It tests who may genuinely occupy the section's role of hadi.

luna: Moses and Aaron are commanded to remain upright and not follow the path of the ignorant; it directly joins steadfast walking with rejecting a divergent route. | terra: Moses and Aaron are told to remain upright and not follow the way of those who do not know. Its command to persist realizes the source dictionary sense of staying in one's course without turning aside.

luna: The verse says God is على صراط مستقيم; this relates the section's straight path to the Lord's own just, steady course, not to a route humans physically walk. | terra: After saying every creature is held by its forelock, Hud says his Lord is upon a straight path. The straightness is the dependable line of divine rule over those moving within it.
terra: The Prophet and those who repent with him are ordered to remain upright as commanded and not overstep. It gives the section's continuing, communal walking its imperative form.
terra: Joseph says he follows the milla of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. As the lead-in to 12:40's upright dīn, it gives an inherited prophetic course rather than an untested ancestral trace.
terra: Joseph calls exclusive worship the upright dīn. The explicit pairing of dīn with q-w-m straightness develops the section's secondary sense of dīn as a sustained way or practice.

luna: The section's path is a community's traveled way; the Prophet calls it “my way” (سبيلي), and says he and his followers call people to God with insight. | terra: The Prophet calls this my way, and includes those who follow him. It supplies both the leading caller and the people walking a shared route behind him.

luna: The verse says every people has a guide; this resonates with the section's hādī as a guide who goes before a group, though the verse does not describe the guide's route. | terra: For every qawm there is a hadi. It gives the source image of a guide who goes before a people and the qawm that follows a concrete Quranic form.

luna: The Messenger brings people from darkness into light and toward the path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy; this places the path within a journey toward a destination. | terra: The Book brings people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission, to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy. Guidance here crosses a real before-and-after passage.

luna: The speakers say God has guided them to their ways and resolve to endure harm; it links received guidance with remaining on a route through difficulty. | terra: The messengers say God has guided us to our paths. Their plural paths are the routes on which they then endure harm, combining guidance and continued travel.

luna: After Iblis promises to mislead people, God says “this is a straight path to Me”; it marks the boundary of the path Iblis cannot redefine. The wording of على has interpretive variation. | terra: God calls this a straight path to Me. It gives the section's hidaya image of a road whose destination is known, rather than direction without arrival.
terra: The ruined settlement remains on an established road. A continuing public route carries a visible sign for those who pass it, connecting road and readable trace.
terra: The two punished peoples are said to lie by a clear imam, an open route. With 15:76 it keeps the road as the place where past signs remain available to travelers.

luna: The verse says the aimed way belongs to God, while some ways are crooked; that is a direct road-level contrast to the section's straight path. | terra: It assigns the direction of the way to God and says some ways are crooked. Its qasd/direction and crooked branch make the section's line, middle, and deviation concrete.

luna: The verse says God placed roads in the earth لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ, so physical routes and being guided are joined as in the section's image. | terra: Mountains, rivers, and roads are placed in the earth so people may find their way; the route is read through the terrain the section calls its signs.

luna: The section's dictionary form for ع ل م includes a mark used to find a road; here عَلامات and stars are explicit means by which people find their way. | terra: Its signs and star-guidance give the Quranic scene for the section's source dictionary sense of alama/alamin as a landmark used to find a road.
luna: Every community receives a messenger commanding worship of God and avoidance of false gods; some are guided and some deserve error, echoing the section's worship/path/straying sequence.
terra: God directs the bee to make homes in mountains, trees, and structures; 16:69 then sends it along made-easy paths. Together they realize the source's paired road-and-home sense of hidaya.

luna: The section's dictionary form الطريق المعبد describes a subdued, easy-to-travel road; the bee is told اسلكي سبل ربك ذللا, to take its Lord's ways made yielding/easy. | terra: The bee is told to follow its Lord's paths made dhululan, made easy or subdued. That concrete traversable path meets the source's secondary image of a softened, tamed walking surface.

luna: The parable contrasts a burden who cannot act with one who commands justice and is on a straight path; it distinguishes a failed guide from someone fit to lead along the road. | terra: In its contrast between two men, the one who commands justice is upon a straight path. The path marks a public, active line of conduct rather than a private claim.

luna: Breaking oaths can make a foot slip after it was firm and turn people from God's way; this concretely reverses the stable, well-trodden road in the section. | terra: It warns that a foot may slip after it was firm, with evil following from turning people away from God's way. The bodily stumble reverses the section's level, steady walking surface.

luna: Abraham is grateful for God's favors, chosen, and guided to a straight path; this binds divine favor and the path as in the section's “those You favored.” | terra: Abraham is chosen and guided to a straight path. His exemplary, grateful course becomes a named antecedent for the community-and-favor strand of the section.

luna: The Prophet is told to follow Abraham's way of worship; this makes a prior community's practiced way an example to follow. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to follow Abraham's upright milla. Following a predecessor's established course continues 16:121's account of Abraham being guided to a straight path.

luna: The command to call people to God's way with wisdom stages the guide's act of showing a route to others. | terra: The Prophet is told to call to his Lord's way with wisdom and good counsel. It makes the guide's forward call to a named path explicit.

luna: The Quran is said to guide to that which is most upright; it supplies a text as a guide toward the section's straightness, though without staging a physical road. | terra: The Quran guides to what is aqwam, more upright. Its q-w-m form gives the section's straightness a superlative moral direction.
luna: The verse states that the guided person benefits himself, while whoever strays bears it; the root ض ل ل named in the section is here contrasted with hidaya's outcome.
luna: On the Day of Resurrection each people is called with its imam; this gives the section's path of a community a concrete image of groups gathered under a leader.
terra: One blind in this world is blind in the next and farther astray in way. The verse gives a contrary navigation image: inability to see signs becomes loss of route.
luna: The verse distinguishes the one God guides from the one He leaves astray; it directly connects the section's guidance/straying pair, though without a path scene.

luna: After realizing they had lost the sign, Moses and his companion turn back, tracking their footprints (آثارهما) to find their way; this concretely matches the section's dictionary sense of a trace used to infer a road.

luna: Moses asks to follow a teacher so he may learn right guidance; it stages the section's image of walking behind someone who knows the way. | terra: Moses asks to follow the servant taught by God so he may learn sound guidance. The act of following a knowing leader supplies an indirect but concrete guide-and-traveler scene.

luna: As in the section's root link between ع ب د and the road, Jesus commands worship and identifies it as a straight path. | terra: Jesus again commands worship of God and calls it the straight path, preserving the section's worship-path equation in its own speech.

luna: The section's hidaya includes a guide leading someone on a way; Abraham tells his father to follow him and promises to guide him to صراطا سويا, an even path. | terra: Abraham tells his father, Follow me, and promises to guide him to a sound path. The speaker literally takes the prior position of the hadi in the section.
terra: It names the prophets and righteous descendants upon whom God bestowed favor. The phrase identifies the favored people of 1:7, before 19:59 shows their successors' break.
terra: After 19:58's favored forebears, successors neglect prayer and follow desires, meeting ghayy. Its break from the favored line makes the community-path reversal explicit.
terra: Moses and Aaron announce that peace is for whoever follows guidance. Their message makes huda something followed behind a pair of messengers.
luna: God spreads the earth and makes roads through it; the section's path is likewise a walkable ground that carries travelers toward where they are going.
luna: Moses is told to travel by night and make a dry path through the sea for the Children of Israel; the verse turns the road into a passable route leading a whole people.

luna: The verse says Pharaoh أضل قومه وما هدى: he led his people astray and did not guide them, a direct reversal of the section's guide who goes ahead for a community. | terra: Pharaoh leads his people astray and does not guide them. This is the counter-image to the hadi who goes ahead of a qawm.

luna: God's guidance is followed, and its follower will neither go astray nor suffer; this gives the section's request for guidance a promised consequence. | terra: When God's guidance comes, whoever follows it will neither go astray nor suffer. It states the direct opposite of the section's dal-lost traveler as sustained following.
terra: The closing question distinguishes the companions of the even path and the guided. It makes straightness and being guided a matter revealed at the route's outcome.
luna: God places mountain passes and roads so people may find their way; this gives the section's navigable path a specific landscape and purpose.

luna: Prophets are made leaders who guide by God's command; this parallels the section's guide who goes ahead of a community, while the verse names their leadership rather than a road. | terra: God makes Abraham's household leaders who guide by His command; their leadership gives a Quranic form to the section's front-going hadi.

luna: The verse says believers were guided to good speech and to the path of the Praiseworthy; it supplies a specific destination on the path. | terra: They are guided to good speech and to the path of the Praiseworthy. The verse preserves the twofold hidaya of right utterance and a route to its Lord.
luna: The verse condemns those who block God's way and the Sacred Mosque; it directly stages a road being obstructed for others.

luna: God guides those who believe to a straight path; this is another direct formulation of the section's requested route. | terra: God is the guide of believers to a straight path. In context, recognizing the revealed truth is what lets them take that route.

luna: Each community is given a rite, then the Prophet is told to invite people while standing on clear guidance; it connects a community's practiced way with a guide's call. | terra: Each community has an appointed rite, while the Prophet stands upon straight guidance. The verse ties a practiced communal dīn to a guiding line.
luna: After 23:52 calls the community one, this verse says its people broke into factions; it contributes the specific fragmentation that opposes a shared road.

luna: The Prophet calls people to a straight path; this directly stages a caller showing others the route. | terra: The Messenger is said to call people to a straight path. The verse supplies the calling, forward-facing guide which the section's hadi image requires.
terra: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter deviate from the straight path. It gives the opposing route of the people to whom 23:73 is calling.

luna: God guides whom He wills to a straight path after sending clear signs; the verse joins discernible signs to finding the route. | terra: After clear signs are sent down, God guides whom He wills to a straight path. The signs are the disclosed markers through which that path is known.

luna: The verse says that if people obey the Messenger they will be guided; it directly links following the guide with finding the way. | terra: The addressees are told that obedience to the Messenger will bring guidance. It makes following a messenger the concrete response to a guide's call.
luna: The regretful person wishes he had taken a way with the Messenger; 25:29 explains that a close companion led him away from the Reminder, so this verse contributes the lost communal route.

luna: The regret in 25:27 continues with the speaker wishing he had not taken a particular person as a close companion; it contributes the choice of companion behind the wrong path described in 25:29.
luna: The speaker says his companion led him astray from the Reminder after it came; 25:27 names the abandoned way with the Messenger, and this verse identifies the misleading guide.
luna: The verse describes people driven on their faces toward Hell and calls them most astray in path; it gives a bodily and destination-based reversal of the straight road.
terra: The Messenger asks no reward except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord. It supplies the route-to-the-Lord side of the section's road-and-home sense.

terra: The servants (ibad) of the Merciful walk gently on the earth. The same worship-family word is joined to a bodily manner of walking, preserving the source's secondary ground-and-service image without replacing the verse's meaning.
luna: After Moses strikes the sea at God's command, it parts into towering sections; 20:77 names the dry path through it, and this verse contributes the opening that makes that route possible.

luna: This verse asks who guides people in the darknesses of land and sea and who sends winds as good tidings; it makes guidance a concrete problem of navigation. | terra: God guides travelers through the darknesses of land and sea. This is a second navigation scene for the landmarks and signs of the section, now with the guide named explicitly.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of هدى is showing someone a way; Moses, traveling toward Midian, asks God to guide him to سواء السبيل, the middle of the way. | terra: Moses asks to be guided to sawāʾ al-sabīl, the level or middle of the road, directly realizing the source dictionary sense of the road's middle.
terra: One who follows desire without guidance from God is called most astray. Desire here is a rival course that pulls a traveler away from shown direction.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of هدى is showing someone the road and its destination; this verse marks a boundary on human guidance by saying the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves, while God guides whom He wills. | terra: The Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; God guides whom He wills. It marks the limit between the human guide who calls ahead and the divine giver of hidaya requested in Fatiha.
luna: Lut's people are accused of cutting off the road; this is a concrete obstruction to travel, reversing the section's passable, walked road.

luna: Those who strive for God are promised guidance to His سبل, plural ways; the verse depicts sustained effort as the way into guidance. | terra: Those who strive for God are promised guidance to His ways. The plural ways are reached through persevering movement, rather than by a detached assertion of belief.
terra: Turn the face toward the upright dīn, the fitra God made. The dīn plus q-w-m pairing develops the section's daily, straightened way of life.
luna: The verse describes people who divided their religion into sects, each faction pleased with itself; it gives the section's “scattering in every direction” a communal form.
terra: Turn the face toward the upright dīn before the irreversible day arrives. It makes keeping one's orientation a sustained preparation, not a bare label.
terra: After refusing parents' call to shirk, one is told to follow the way of one who turns to God. It specifies a human route to follow while setting a boundary for inherited obedience.
terra: Luqman tells his son to be moderate in his walking. The concrete gait gives a small bodily analogue to the section's middle and un-deviating route.
terra: They prefer what they found their fathers practicing when called to revelation, even if Satan calls them toward the Blaze. It continues 31:15's true way with its contrary inherited following.

luna: Leaders among the people guide by God's command after patience; this gives a specific community-leading counterpart to the section's hâdî. | terra: Patient and certain Israelites are made leaders guiding by God's command. The verse binds ongoing steadfastness to a community's guiding leaders.

luna: People in Hell say they obeyed their leaders and were led away from the way; this is a direct warning about following a community's guide in the wrong direction. | terra: At judgment people say their chiefs and great ones made them lose the way. The community's leaders here do the opposite of the preceding guide.
terra: Those given knowledge see the revelation as truth that guides to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy. It pairs a readable sign with the road it discloses.
luna: A connected chain of towns is set between Sheba and blessed towns, with travel measured between them; this places markers and repeated journeys along a route.

luna: The people ask for longer distances between travel stops and are then scattered; 34:18 supplies the linked route, while this verse contributes the rejection of its connected stages and the resulting dispersion.
terra: Its declaration that Muhammad is a messenger supplies the guide-speaker; the immediately following 36:4 gives that messenger's own standing on the straight path.
terra: It says the messenger is upon a straight path. Its own contribution is to locate the leader announced in 36:3 on the route he communicates.

luna: This command tells the criminals to separate on Judgment Day; 36:60–62 then contrasts their separation with worship on the straight path and Satan's diversion, while this verse contributes the separation. | terra: The criminals are told to separate today. Its own judgment-day partition completes the route boundary stated in 36:61, rather than merely repeating its worship command.
luna: The command not to worship Satan because he is an enemy leads into 36:61's identification of worship as the straight path; this verse contributes the specific rival object of worship.

luna: Here the source section's root ع ب د retains its Quranic sense: “worship Me” is directly identified as a straight path, as in the section's worship-and-road sequence. | terra: The divine address says Worship Me; this is a straight path. It directly links the fifth-ayah worship to the sixth-ayah road.

luna: After the command to worship on a straight path in 36:61, this verse says Satan led many astray; it names the road's opposite as being misled. | terra: The devil has led a great multitude astray. It names the destructive guide and scattered human mass that follow the worship-path warning of 36:61.

luna: The preceding command gathers the wrongdoers with those they worshipped; 37:23 then directs this gathered group to Hell's path, and this verse supplies the collective procession's starting point.

luna: The section ends with guidance and the straight path; here the gathered wrongdoers are led to صراط الجحيم, the same guiding action and path with an inverted destination. | terra: The command to guide them to the path of Hell reverses both hidaya and the destination of the straight path: the same road-language reaches the contrary home.
luna: The verse says the deniers hurry along their fathers' traces (آثار); its context says those fathers were astray, making inherited footprints a specific false path.
terra: Abraham says he is going to his Lord and that He will guide him. The journey makes guidance point toward the Lord as a known destination.
terra: Moses and Aaron are guided to a straight path after receiving the clear Book, linking a named pair of leaders, scripture, and a traveled line.
luna: The section's dictionary form “middle of the road” is made explicit by سواء الصراط; the disputants ask for guidance to the path's center while warning against excess.
terra: David is warned not to follow desire, lest it lead him away from God's way. Desire is the force that bends a ruler off the line he must keep straight.

luna: Pharaoh claims, “I guide you only to the way of right guidance”; in its context this is a ruler's claim, exposing the danger of a false guide on the road. | terra: Pharaoh claims that he guides his people only to the way of right conduct. Its false guide-speech is answered by the believer's genuine Follow me in 40:38.

luna: A believer in Pharaoh's household says “follow me” and promises guidance to سبيل الرشاد; it stages a guide leading a community along a way. | terra: The believing man tells his qawm, Follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct. This is the section's guide-ahead-of-a-community scene in direct speech.
terra: The Messenger declares the one God and commands people to be upright toward Him. The imperative gives the section's straight continuation a direct address.

luna: Thamud were shown guidance but preferred blindness over it; the verse presents a community rejecting the route made visible to them. | terra: Thamud are shown guidance but prefer blindness to it. The refusal turns the section's readable signs into a chosen failure of orientation.
terra: Those who say our Lord is God and then remain upright receive the angels' reassurance. Straightness is presented as a course sustained after the first confession.

luna: The verse says God guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him; it relates turning toward a destination to the section's guidance request, without describing a road. | terra: The commanded dīn is to be established and not divided within. Its continuity and refusal of fragmentation parallel the section's single shared way against scattered groups.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to invite people and remain upright as commanded; this connects calling others with steadfastness on the straight way. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to call and remain upright as commanded. It makes his own firmness part of his leading call to the route.

luna: The Prophet is described as guiding to صراط مستقيم; this directly joins the section's guide who goes before with the route he leads people toward. | terra: The Prophet is said to guide to a straight path, directly joining prophetic speech and the section's front-going hadi.
luna: The earth is made a resting place and roads are placed in it لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ; this directly parallels the section's paths made for finding one's way.

luna: The people claim to be guided by following their fathers' آثار (traces); it contrasts inherited footprints with the section's path of those truly favored. | terra: The speakers claim that they found their fathers on a community and are guided by their traces. Their inherited footprints form a contrary test for the section's already-walked path.

luna: The verse continues the claim in 43:22 by showing earlier messengers met with the same appeal to ancestral practice; it gives the refusal context while 43:22 itself supplies the trace-following claim. | terra: The same claim is repeated of later affluent communities: they follow the traces of their fathers. It makes custom's repeated track a possible substitute for actual guidance.
terra: When a messenger asks whether even better guidance than the fathers' traces has come, the communities reject it. This completes 43:22-23's warning that a repeated track may refuse correction.
luna: Satanic companions turn people away from the way while their victims think they are guided; it shows false guidance as deviation masked as direction.

luna: The command to hold fast to revelation is followed by “you are on a straight path”; it makes staying with guidance an act of remaining on the road. | terra: The Prophet is told to hold fast to revelation because he is upon a straight path. Holding and remaining on it make the route continuous rather than momentary.
luna: The verse commands people to follow and calls that a straight path; its context identifies Jesus, so it adds a speaker-specific invitation to the path beside 43:64.

luna: This verse repeats the section's precise conjunction: God is Lord, so worship Him; that worship is called a straight path. | terra: Jesus' command to worship God is again completed by this is a straight path; its repeated formulation makes worship the route rather than merely a doctrine.

luna: The Prophet is set upon a law and way (شريعة), commanded to follow it, and warned against the desires of the ignorant; this directly joins a prescribed route, following it, and refusing a divergent path. | terra: The Prophet is placed on a sharia, a way of command, and told to follow it rather than desires. Its way becomes the daily dīn-like practice that resists departure.
terra: Those who say our Lord is God and remain upright need not fear or grieve. The verse repeats the enduring straight stance as a lived course.

luna: The jinn report a scripture that guides إلى الحق وإلى طريق مستقيم; the exact route language makes this a direct guidance parallel. | terra: The jinn describe the revealed Book as guiding to truth and a straight path. It gives the Book the road-disclosing function of the section's signs.

luna: People turn back after guidance has become clear, and Satan makes this seem attractive; this is a specific reversal of staying on the guided road. | terra: After guidance has become clear, some turn back on their heels. The bodily reversal gives a concrete opposite to staying in the course one has taken.
luna: Those who disbelieve and bar people from God's way after guidance is clear are described as opposing the Messenger; it shows a known path deliberately blocked.

luna: The verse says God will guide the Prophet to صراطا مستقيما; it is a direct statement of the guidance requested in the section. | terra: Along with forgiveness and completing favor, God guides the Prophet to a straight path. Favor and the route meet here as they do in Fatiha 1:7.
luna: After promising gains and protection, the verse says God will guide the believers to a straight path; it connects concrete events to their route.
luna: God promises believers a light by which they walk; this connects the section's wayfinding signs with actual movement along a route.
luna: When Moses's people deviated, God made their hearts deviate; the verb زاغوا names turning away from the straight course, a direct boundary against remaining on it.

luna: The source image is a road walked by feet; this verse contrasts someone walking fallen on his face with one walking upright on a straight path. | terra: It compares one walking face-down, stumbling, with one walking upright upon a straight path. The physical traveler makes the section's path image visible in reverse and fulfillment.
luna: The earth is made a spread-out surface so people can travel its broad roads; this closely stages the section's walked, passable road.

luna: The verse describes people who استقاموا على الطريقة, staying upright on the way; it directly matches the section's third hidaya sense of continuing without leaving the path. | terra: Had people remained steadfast upon the way, they would have received abundant water. Its conditional uses a path as something one can stay on and receive provision along.

luna: God shows the human the way, then the person is either grateful or ungrateful; the verse makes the guided road a point of choice, as the section's path contrasts the guided and straying. | terra: God says He showed the human being the way, whether grateful or ungrateful. The shown route has the same active disclosure requested by ihdina.

luna: God makes the way easy for the human; this resonates specifically with the section's dictionary image of a road subdued by repeated walking, though السبيل here may mean life's way or the passage of birth.

luna: The verse says God showed the human the two high roads (النجدين); this presents the section's straight path against an alternative route. | terra: God says He showed the two high roads. The disclosed alternatives give the request for a guided way its moral fork.
terra: After the two high roads of 90:10, the person has not undertaken the steep ascent. Its difficult pass gives the disclosed route a concrete walking surface and cost.

luna: The section reads ضالا فهدى as a seeker found and guided; because ضالًّا can be understood more broadly than losing a physical road, this is a qualified root-level reversal linking ض ل ل and ه د ي. | terra: God finds the Prophet dāll and guides him. The compact reversal is the source's hidaya-versus-dalal pair, with the latter overcome rather than inhabited.
terra: The command to worship sincerely is called the dīn al-qayyima. The source's dīn and q-w-m senses meet here in an enacted, upright practice.

luna: The section names the secondary dictionary sense of دِين as a habitual way of acting; لكم دينكم ولي دين uses the same word for each side's religious way, but the link to repeated daily walking is interpretive rather than explicit.
